To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a technology system that is designed to be easy, useful, and engaging leads to rich use, which in turn leads to job performance.
(1) system design principles influence the use and net benefits of information technology and (2) rich use influences job performance.
the proposed framework and propositions can guide future work on technology use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to design systems that are effective and efficient in terms of use and net benefits.
understanding how design principles affect technology use and performance outcomes.
understanding and improving the design of information systems and technologies to increase their use, and to enhance the performance and well-being of the users of these systems and technologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the framework presented in the paper is useful in that it provides a basis for future research on the relationship between design principles and technology use and performance.
this study contributes to our understanding of the relationships between system design, use, and net benefits by integrating three streams of research.
the framework and propositions we present in this paper are a first attempt to provide an integrative view of the relationships among system design principles, use, and impacts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose that the use of technology should be studied as a process, not as a single event, and we suggest that the design principles that are most effective for promoting technology use and net benefits are those that are tailored to the individual and that promote a rich use of technology.
the design principles are important for the success of a system, and that the use of a system is an important mechanism through which the design principles lead to the success of a technology.
the framework provides a foundation to integrate and extend the literature on IS success, technology acceptance, and design principles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the proposed framework to better understand how to design information systems so that they are more likely to be adopted, used richly, and lead to net benefits.
technology use is a complex process that requires a multi-faceted approach to be studied.
we can use a set of design principles as a guide to design information systems that are more likely to be used and lead to better job performance.
